name: Coral bleaching
value: No global event; Caribbean heat stress
summary: No global bleaching event declared; El Niño heat stress forecast across the Caribbean into November
state: NOAA experts judged the fourth global bleaching event to have ended in mid-2025 (GCRMN, 8 Jun). NOAA's August outlook gave a greater than 70% chance of Alert Level 1 heat stress across most of the Caribbean by early November (GCRMN, 14 Aug), and the Florida Keys were at Alert Level 4 on 25 Aug with bleaching in 23 of 27 observer reports (Mote). No confirmed regional mass bleaching or new global event was found as of 8 Nov, so the level stays Normal pending field reports.
for_you: Bleaching mainly threatens reef ecosystems and the fishing and tourism communities that rely on them, especially in the Caribbean.
rubric_hit: Normal: no global bleaching event in progress; regional mass bleaching not confirmed as of 8 Nov

sources.title: GCRMN — Fourth global coral bleaching event has likely ended
Mote Marine Laboratory — Florida Keys coral condition report, 25 Aug

why: Reefs support a quarter of marine species and coastal economies; mass bleaching is a direct sign of ocean heat stress.
drivers: Marine heatwaves, El Niño, warming trend.

rubric.alert: Bleaching extent at record levels with active new alerts in the past month.
rubric.watch: Global bleaching event in progress, or regional mass bleaching.
rubric.normal: No global bleaching event in progress.
